claims.content: The C2 JU manages track identity classification by assigning, exchanging, and resolving standard identity states (Pending, Unknown, Assumed Friend, Friend, Neutral, Suspect, Hostile) for tracks in accordance with MIL-STD-6016B definitions and difference resolution rules.

goal.raw_text: The C2 JU manages track identity classification by assigning, exchanging, and resolving standard identity states (Pending, Unknown, Assumed Friend, Friend, Neutral, Suspect, Hostile) for tracks in accordance with MIL-STD-6016B definitions and difference resolution rules.

claims.content: C2 JU
The C2 JU has correlated local sensor data.
Track identity as defined in paragraph 4.4.2.1 is exchanged.
The Platform and platform activity fields are defined in the message section of this volume.
The C2 JU detects an identity difference where its locally held track identity differs from the identity reported on the interface.

trigger.raw_text: The C2 JU detects an identity difference where its locally held track identity differs from the identity reported on the interface.

claims.content: The C2 JU detects an identity difference between locally held track identity and identity reported on the interface.
Interface procedures recognize and resolve ID differences; all IUs should hold the same common ID for a given track.

If an ID conflict exists (difference cannot be automatically accepted or rejected), the difference is presented to operators for evaluation, potentially requiring voice coordination for final resolution.

Identity differences are processed according to Table 4.7-2 framework, which specifies actions: NO ACTION (0), OPERATOR ALERT requiring manual action (1), ACCEPT received ID as local ID (2), or REJECT received ID (3).
The R² unit transmits the changed identity in the appropriate surveillance message at the next transmit opportunity with Identity Difference Indicator set to value 0.
All other interface units report the changed ID in a J7.0 (ACT = 1) Difference Report message.
The controlling unit of the track automatically rejects received ID data and transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 1) message with own unit data and Controlling Unit Indicator field set to value 1.

Non-R² units resolve ID differences in accordance with Table 4.7-2; if directed to automatically accept or reject, the system updates local ID or transmits J7.0 (ACT = 1) with local data respectively; otherwise, the operator is alerted and resolves the conflict.

Under specific conditions (PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator set to 1, new identity is Friend, locally held identity is not Hostile), the C² JU may elect to automatically accept changes in Identity received in a track report.

If the locally held Environment/Category of a track differs from that received in a J3.X or J7.0 (ACT = 1) message, the operator shall be alerted, even if the received Environment/Category is not implemented.
If local data and received data differ as to whether the Track Number (TN) is assigned to a point or to a track, the operator shall be alerted.

When an ID conflict exists (difference cannot be automatically accepted or rejected), the difference must be presented to operators for evaluation, potentially requiring voice coordination for final resolution.
Receipt of ID data on a TN for which the receiving JU does not have R² and local positional data is not held will automatically be accepted, and the remote ID placed in the database for retention.

A controlling unit receiving a J7.0 (ACT = 1) message reporting a different ID for a locally-controlled track shall automatically reject the received ID and originate a J7.0 (ACT = 1) message with local ID data and Controlling Unit Indicator set to 1.
All interface units receiving a J7.0 (ACT = 1) message from the controlling unit (with Controlling Unit Indicator set to 1) shall automatically accept the remote data for database update.

If the R² JU is directed to automatically accept the remote ID, the system shall update the local database and report the new track data in the appropriate surveillance message at the next transmit opportunity.
If the R² JU is directed to automatically reject the remote ID, the system shall discard the message and continue reporting the track with local data.
Identity differences are processed according to Table 4.7-2, which specifies actions: NO ACTION (0), OPERATOR ALERT (1), ACCEPT received ID (2), or REJECT received ID (3).

In three specific cases marked with '*' in Table 4.7-2 (Pending vs Hostile, Unknown vs Hostile, Suspect vs Hostile), systems may have a feature to automatically accept received ID as local ID instead of requiring operator alert.

If conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction, the operator shall be alerted and may either change the local ID/Exercise Indicator to allow automatic correlation, or transmit an ID Difference Report to allow automatic correlation if the remote ID or Exercise Indicator is changed.

If an ID conflict exists (difference cannot be automatically accepted or rejected), the difference must be presented to operators for evaluation, potentially requiring voice coordination for final resolution.

When a controlling unit receives a surveillance message with ID different from local data, it shall automatically reject the received ID data and transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 1) message with own unit data and Controlling Unit Indicator set to value 1.
If the R² JU is directed to automatically reject the remote ID, the system shall discard the message and the track shall continue to be reported with local data.
If the locally held Environment/Category differs from received data, the operator shall be alerted even if the received Environment/Category is not implemented.
If local data and received data differ as to whether the Track Number is assigned to a point or to a track, the operator shall be alerted.
All Interface Units (IUs) hold the same common Identity (ID) for a given track after resolution.
The R² unit transmits the changed identity in the appropriate surveillance message at the next transmit opportunity with the Identity Difference Indicator set to value 0.
All other interface units report the changed ID in a J7.0 (ACT = 1) Difference Report message.

The controlling unit of the track automatically rejects received ID data that differs from local data and transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 1) message with own unit data and Controlling Unit Indicator field set to value 1.
All interface units receiving a J7.0 (ACT = 1) message from the controlling unit (with Controlling Unit Indicator set to 1) automatically accept the remote data for database update.

If the R² JU is directed to automatically accept the remote ID, the system updates the local database and reports the new track data in the appropriate surveillance message at the next transmit opportunity.
If the R² JU is directed to automatically reject the remote ID, the system discards the message and the track continues to be reported with local data.
